title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District
area: Allegheny County, including the City of Pittsburgh and its eastern and southern suburbs.

context.text: Summer Lee defeated William Parker 81.2% to 18.8% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. James Hayes was unopposed in the Republican primary. Lee defeated Hayes in the 2024 general election.

summary.text: Summer Lee is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 12th District, first elected in 2022. An attorney and organizer from the Mon Valley, she served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2019 until she entered Congress. Her official site lists her committees as Judiciary and Education and Workforce, and she campaigns on reproductive rights, gun-violence prevention, and affordable housing.

background.text: Born in North Braddock, Pennsylvania, in 1987 and raised in the Mon Valley, where she attended Woodland Hills public schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Pennsylvania State University in 2009 and a J.D. from Howard University in 2015.
Worked as a summer intern with the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund and the Office of the Attorney General of the District of Columbia.

According to her campaign website, she worked as an organizer on voter mobilization for the Pennsylvania Democratic Party, including in 2016, and in 2017 led an initiative to change the makeup of the Woodland Hills School Board.

Won election to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2018, defeating a 20-year incumbent in the primary with more than 67% of the vote, according to her campaign website. She served from 2019 and was the first Black woman from Western Pennsylvania in the legislature.
Elected to Congress in 2022 and, per her official biography, is the first Black woman elected to Congress from Pennsylvania. She won re-election in 2024, defeating James Hayes.
Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary and the Committee on Education and Workforce, according to her official site.

Her official biography says she has worked on getting money out of politics, environmental justice and criminal legal reform, and credits her office with bringing more than $2.7 billion to the district. She won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 81.2% of the vote over William Parker, and lives in Swissvale, according to WESA's 2024 voter guide.

priorities.text: Says Congress must protect federal abortion rights, repeal the Hyde Amendment, and pass legislation such as the Women's Health Protection Act and the EACH Act.
priorities.quote: We need to protect reproductive rights at the federal level. And Congress must not only safeguard the federal right to abortion, but also repeal laws like the Hyde amendment.

priorities.text: Says gun violence in western Pennsylvania requires both an assault-weapons ban and expanded background checks, as well as investment in underfunded communities to address the root causes of street violence.

positions.summary: Supports codifying federal abortion rights, repealing the Hyde Amendment, and ending the federal criminalization of abortion; supports expanding the Supreme Court in response to its abortion rulings.
positions.quote: The right-wing extremists on the Supreme Court have gutted our constitutional right to abortion care, and Congress must do everything in its power to protect this fundamental right.

positions.summary: Supports an assault-weapons ban, expanded background checks, and ending legal protections for gun manufacturers.
positions.quote: We need an assault weapons ban, expanded background checks, end protections for corporate gun manufacturers and bold gun-safety legislation.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 2025-2026 Congress.
Joined Reps. Frost and Mfume in pressing the ATF director for answers on Trump administration rollbacks of gun-safety regulations, May 2026.
Elected to the Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District in 2022 and re-elected in 2024, defeating James Hayes.

candidates.name: James Hayes

summary.text: James Hayes is a businessman and economist with degrees from Georgetown, Princeton, the University of Chicago and Case Western Reserve who worked for the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond. He was the Republican nominee in 2024 and lost to incumbent Summer Lee, and is running again in 2026. He campaigns on reducing regulation, school choice, and law-enforcement support.

background.text: Born in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Conestoga Valley High School. PoliticsPA reports he is the son of a union steelworker and that a United Steelworkers scholarship first sent him to college.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University in 1983, a graduate degree from Princeton University in 1985 and one from the University of Chicago in 1989. WESA's 2024 voter guide lists them as a B.S.F.S. in international economics, an M.P.A. in economics and policy, and an M.B.A., plus a D.B.A. in management from Case Western Reserve University.

Spent about 30 years in finance and industry, including six years at the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond and, per PoliticsPA, top positions at Fortune 500 companies. WESA listed his 2024 occupation as chief financial officer.

Ran for the 12th District as the Republican nominee in 2024, his first campaign, and lost to Lee. WESA reported he entered the race after his son was killed in a homicide that was then unsolved. He lived in Shadyside, Pittsburgh, as of 2024.
Advanced unopposed from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 23,760 votes.

priorities.text: Says he supports ending overregulation that he says is costing the region jobs and causing industry to leave, and supports school choice to improve educational outcomes regardless of zip code.
priorities.quote: He will support ending the overregulation that is costing our region valuable jobs and causing industry to flee.

priorities.text: Lists economic growth and energy independence, border security, access to quality education, and public safety and support of law enforcement as areas of passion.

positions.summary: Supports implementing school choice so that children are not "condemned to a poor education because of their zip code."
positions.quote: Children should not be condemned to a poor education because of their zip code and we must implement school choice to provide the incentives to improve outcomes across the educational spectrum.

positions.summary: Supports Israel and its right to defend itself.
positions.quote: He supports Israel and its right to defend itself, opposes excessive government spending and will work to restore balance, accountability and civility to our government.

positions.summary: Says he supports law enforcement and will work to ensure officers have the tools needed to keep communities safe.
positions.quote: James supports our law enforcement and will work to ensure they have the tools they need to keep our communities safe.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions are drawn from a 2023 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (Hayes has not completed an updated 2026 survey). A current personal campaign website was not confirmed reachable within the research budget.
